{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI and Publish

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
    # Only trigger for changes inside portpy/
    paths:
      - 'portpy/**'
  pull_request:
    # Only trigger for PRs touching portpy/
    paths:
      - 'portpy/**'
  release:
    types: [published]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # CPU-only torch (small wheel, no CUDA) so the portpy.ai tests run
          pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
          pip install .[test]

      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest -v --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings

  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    if: github.event_name == 'release' && github.event.action == 'published'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

      - name: Install build tools
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install build twine

      - name: Build package
        run: python -m build

      - name: Publish to PyPI
        env:
          TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
        run: twine upload dist/*
",
  "rationale": "Add pip dependency caching to both test and publish jobs using actions/cache@v4. The cache key is based on pyproject.toml (the project's dependency lockfile) to ensure cache invalidation when dependencies change. This optimization is supported by experimental evidence showing ~9% elapsed time reduction for a similar Python workflow (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2). The change preserves all existing test coverage and build steps, only adding cache restore/save steps before dependency installation.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}

```yaml
      - 'portpy/**'
  release:
    types: [published]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # CPU-only torch (small wheel, no CUDA) so the portpy.ai tests run
          pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
          pip install .[test]

      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest -v --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings

  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    if: github.event_name == 'release' && github.event.action == 'published'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install build tools
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install build twine

      - name: Build package
        run: python -m build

      - name: Publish to PyPI
        env:
          TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
        run: twine upload dist/*
```

The workflow has two jobs: test and publish. The test job installs dependencies (including torch from a custom index) and runs pytest. The publish job builds and publishes to PyPI on release.

Now, look at the evidence. There are several experiment examples and pattern catalog entries. The patterns include caching, fail-fast, cancel stale, etc.

The workflow currently does not have any caching for pip dependencies. The test job installs dependencies every run. This is a good candidate for caching pip dependencies.

The workflow uses pyproject.toml and requirements.txt. There's a pyproject.toml file in the repository context.
